approval.basis: Owner accepted the desktop/mobile before-after proposal and explicitly instructed implementation on 2026-10-23

scope.population: Existing adult pathway, age >=18 years; no new upper-age threshold
required_biological_data: serum creatinine with mg/dL or µmol/L
scope.age_policy: cg_norm only uses floor(exact age in years); no rounding to nearest year; canonical months/DOB/exact age and historical results are preserved
scope.clinical_impact: New cg_norm results with nonzero stored months may change; this is explicit input precision policy, not correction of a demonstrated fractional-age equation error
equations_unchanged: Du Bois coefficient 0.007184 with kg^0.425 and cm^0.725
CG times 1.73 divided by unrounded adult BSA
Final display rounding to integer only after indexing
scope.interpretation: eCrCl remains distinct from eGFR; no universal numeric norm, category G or >=90 threshold added
scope.assumptions: Stable kidney function and no suspected AKI remain stated assumptions when no contrary facts are known; known AKI or rapid creatinine change still block; no new IDMS/IFCC question for CG
exclusions: No automatic ideal/adjusted body weight substitution
No retrospective recomputation of stored results

synthetic_regression.contracts: No source-free copied formula test; regression calls actual production calculation/adapter/UI. Test results are recorded in PR verification rather than inferred from this source review.

inference_limits: Indexing CG changes scale and unit, not its target or validation.
Current sources do not justify automatic G categories or a universal ≥90 normal threshold for this application output.
No source found for a universal reference interval is not proof that no local or population-specific CrCl range can exist.
Height remains necessary for this selected Du Bois indexed output; dropping it would change the output or require an unsupported assumption.

Completed years are a defensible explicit age policy for a minimal adult CG form, supported by an official contextual precedent; it is not a correction of a demonstrated medical error in fractional age.
Removing optional months requires changing actual cg_norm age use, preserving months for other equations and historical records, and disclosing that new numerical results may change.
